title: Quarter-wave TiO2/SiO2 dichroic stack centered at 550 nm, 24 layers, 45 degree incidence
scientific_hypothesis: A 12-pair alternating TiO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack with optical thickness centered at 550 nm will produce a high-reflectance stopband covering 450-650 nm while allowing high transmittance at 700-1000 nm, even at 45 degree incidence.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create constructive interference for reflection at the design wavelength when each layer has optical thickness n*t = lambda_0/4. The stopband width scales with the index contrast ratio. TiO2/SiO2 provides high contrast (~2.4/1.46), which should give a wide enough stopband to cover the visible range while the NIR falls outside the stopband.
proposed_topology: 24 layers alternating TiO2/SiO2 starting with TiO2: [TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2, TiO2, SiO2] on fused silica substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers
initialization from quarter-wave formula at 550 nm center wavelength
soft_objectives: maximize average reflectance in 450-650 nm band
maximize average transmittance in 700-1000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds: TiO2 layers 25-150 nm, SiO2 layers 40-200 nm to stay within practical deposition ranges
all layers must be positive thickness
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance stopbands centered at the design wavelength where each layer has optical thickness lambda_0/4
Stopband width increases with the ratio of high-to-low refractive index
At oblique incidence, the effective optical thickness decreases by cos(theta) factor, shifting the stopband to shorter wavelengths
S and P polarizations experience different effective indices at oblique incidence, which can split the stopband
TiO2 has refractive index approximately 2.4-2.6 in visible range, SiO2 approximately 1.45-1.46
expected_advantages: Structured quarter-wave initialization should converge faster than random thickness starting points
Periodic structure is manufacturable and well-understood in thin-film practice
12 pairs should provide sufficient reflectance in the stopband based on recalled design rules
known_risks: I am uncertain about the exact refractive index values of TiO2 and SiO2 across 450-1000 nm - these are measured data that must come from the material registry, not assumed
I am uncertain whether 550 nm is the optimal center wavelength - the visible band is 450-650 nm, so 550 nm is the arithmetic center, but the optimal center for maximum band coverage may differ
I am uncertain about the polarization behavior at 45 degrees - the request does not specify polarization state, and s/p splitting could degrade performance for unpolarized light
I am uncertain whether 12 pairs is optimal - more pairs increase reflectance but may narrow the transmission band; fewer pairs may not achieve sufficient visible reflectance
The 50 nm transition band (650-700 nm) is very narrow - I do not know from memory whether a quarter-wave stack can achieve sharp enough cutoff
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate using alternating TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao) layers. Layer sequence: TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao) (24 layers total, starting with TiO2 (Siefke)). Incident angle is 45 degrees. Wavelength bands: maximize reflectance in 450-650 nm, maximize transmittance in 700-1000 nm. Initialize layer thicknesses from quarter-wave formula at 550 nm center wavelength (TiO2 (Siefke) nominal thickness = 550/(4*n_TiO2 (Siefke)), SiO2 (Gao) nominal thickness = 550/(4*n_SiO2 (Gao))), then optimize all 24 thicknesses independently within bounds: TiO2 (Siefke) layers 25-150 nm, SiO2 (Gao) layers 40-200 nm. Use coherent transfer matrix method for unpolarized light (average of s and p polarization results). Material optical constants (n, k) are read from the registry datasets for TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao) - do not assume values.
